ann_28.text: This part acts on only 8 of 242 training patients (3%), women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise; 7 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 62-year-old woman with chest pain on exercise, a normal resting ECG, a flat ST segment and resting blood pressure of 145 mm Hg), it raises the predicted risk from about 12% to about 92% (the model has little data on this, n = 8).
Through it, chest pain brought on by exercise raises that patient's predicted risk from about 12% to about 92%, and being a woman rather than a man does the same.
Signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG switch it off, bringing the risk back down from about 92% to about 12%.

Across the whole model, being a woman lowers the predicted risk, more so if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy (from about 33% to about 1%, against about 23% to about 1% otherwise) and if exercise does not bring on chest pain (to about 1%, against about 4% with it).
Chest pain on exercise adds to the predicted risk only if the resting ECG shows no left ventricular hypertrophy, and a typical patient stays at about 23% either way.

ann_29.text: This part barely changes the predictions.
Through it, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG raise a typical patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 24%.

ann_30.text: This part acts on 111 of 242 training patients (46%), all of them patients with a flat ST segment; 72 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 58-year-old man with a flat ST segment, 1.2 mm of ST depression, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG and a reversible thallium defect), it raises the predicted risk from about 96% to about 97%.
Through it, a flat ST segment raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 29%.
The rise from a flat ST segment is a little larger if exercise brings on chest pain, though for a typical patient it goes from about 23% to about 80% either way.

Through this part, being a woman, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG and chest pain on exercise each barely move the predicted risk of the typical patient it acts on, which stays at about 97%.

ann_31.text: For a typical patient, the model gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (about 1%), non-anginal chest pain (about 2%) or atypical angina (about 12%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 23%).

Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same: going from 0 to 2 vessels raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 96%, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher.
A flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 80%, and a reversible defect on the thallium scan to about 47%.

More ST depression on exercise, higher cholesterol and older age each raise it steadily: from about 16% at 0 mm to about 50% at 2.8 mm, from about 13% at 193 mg/dL to about 45% at 308 mg/dL, and from about 17% at 42 to about 28% at 66 years.
Being a woman lowers it from about 23% to about 1%, and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG raise it to about 33%; both also act through the flat ST segment part.
A higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 26% at 118 to about 21% at 175 beats per minute, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers it to about 19%.
A fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 8% and a downsloping ST segment raises it to about 27% (the model has little data on this, n = 15 and 17).

Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same (from about 23% at 0 to about 96% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher); more ST depression on exercise (from about 16% at 0 mm to about 50% at 2.8 mm), higher cholesterol (from about 13% at 193 mg/dL to about 45% at 308 mg/dL) and older age (from about 17% at 42 to about 28% at 66 years) raise it steadily, and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 26% at 118 to about 21% at 175 beats per minute.

Sex, the resting ECG and the slope of the ST segment also enter this sum, and act through the part below as well: across the whole model, being a woman lowers a typical patient's risk from about 23% to about 1%, a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 80%, and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG to about 33%.

Two less common results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 15 and 17): a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the risk to about 8%, and a downsloping ST segment raises it to about 27%.

This part combines the slope of the ST segment with a smaller part that reads sex, the resting ECG and chest pain on exercise, and acts on 111 of 242 training patients, all of them with a flat ST segment; 72 of them had heart disease.
Through it, a flat ST segment raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 29%.

The smaller part inside it switches on only for women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise, and raises the predicted risk of the typical such patient from about 12% to about 92% (the model has little data on this, n = 8).

Across the whole model, being a woman lowers the predicted risk more when the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy: it falls from about 33% to about 1% with those signs, against about 23% to about 1% without them.

ann_28.original: Hypothesis: node 665 is a three-way AND gate that fires only for women (sex:0 set) with exercise-induced angina (exang:0 unset, i.e. exang=yes) and no left-ventricular hypertrophy on resting ECG (restecg:2 unset). The restecg:2 chain 2349 -> 2771 never leaves the ReLU linear region on standardized one-hot inputs (2349 in [1.15,3.11], 2771 in [1.99,3.72]), so the gate collapses exactly to relu(1.41 sex:0 - 1.71 exang:0 - 1.18 restecg:2 - 3.39). Evidence (train, n=242): pre-activation max is 2.117, reached only when all three conditions hold; removing any one condition drives it negative (no female: -0.86; no exang: -2.53; LVH present: -0.24). The gate is active on 8/242 rows (3.3%), always at the single value 2.117, and 7 of those 8 are positive cases. Closed form matches the forward pass (check_explanation closed-form err 0.0049, numeric err 0).
ann_28.proposed: A part that acts only on 8 women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise and raises their predicted risk from about 12% to about 92%; signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG switch it off.

ann_29.original: Hypothesis: node 2447 is an always-active affine relay of restecg:2 (LVH on resting ECG). Evidence (train): pre-activation in [0.485, 2.516], so the ReLU never clips; through its 0.026 output weight it adds 0.026*1.02 = 0.026 per SD of restecg:2 to the logit (logit-term SD 0.026 vs total logit SD 4.3), i.e. it is practically inert and simply nudges the direct restecg:2 weight from 0.224 to 0.250. Closed-form err 0.0083 (3-s.f. rounding).
ann_29.proposed: A part that barely changes the predictions; through it, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG raise a typical patient's predicted risk from about 23% to about 24%.

ann_30.original: Hypothesis: serial composition H(G(sex:0, exang:0, restecg:2), slope:2). Node 3598 = relu(1.51 slope:2 + 1.05 G - 0.76) and node 1650 = relu(1.29 G + 1.31*3598 - 0.73). Because G takes only the values 0 or 2.117 and slope:2 is binary, 1650 has exactly four regimes on train: G=0 & slope not flat -> 0 (n=131, 27% positive); G=0 & flat slope (slope:2) -> 0.446 (n=103, 63% positive); G on & slope not flat -> 2.097 (n=1, negative); G on & flat slope -> 6.092 (n=7, all positive). So without the gate it is a small additional flat-ST-slope bonus (+0.34 logit after the 0.772 output weight, on top of the direct slope:2 weight); with the gate it amplifies the female-exertional-angina signal, and the flat-slope ReLU 3598 makes the two conditions super-additive (6.09 vs 0.45+2.10). Evidence: activation_profile on node 1650 (train): active 45.9%, mean 0.375, SD 1.018, max 6.092; values confirmed by local forward pass.
ann_30.proposed: A part that acts on patients with a flat ST segment and raises their predicted risk: through it a flat ST segment takes a typical patient from about 23% to about 29%, and the typical patient it acts on from about 96% to about 97%.

ann_31.original: Hypothesis: additive composition. The logit z of node 0 is a linear score over 17 direct standardized inputs (dominated by ca 1.93, sex:1 1.67, cp:4 1.21, slope:2 1.05, chol 0.72, oldpeak 0.71) plus 0.772 x flat_slope_amplifier plus 0.026 x restecg2_relay; 7 inputs (trestbps, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:1, exang:1, thal:3, thal:4) are disconnected. get_formula shows node 0 as ReLU, but for this binary task the model output is sigmoid(z) on the pre-activation (compute_performance train AUC 0.945 equals AUC of z; sigmoid(relu(z)) would give 0.912). Evidence (train, n=242, local forward passes): direct-linear logit SD 4.33 vs amplifier term SD 0.79 vs relay term SD 0.026. Dropping the amplifier term lowers train AUC 0.945 -> 0.930 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.868; the direct linear part alone gives AUC 0.931. So the network is essentially logistic regression plus one sparse nonlinear correction: a flat-slope bonus (+0.34 logit) and a large boost (+4.7 logit) for the 7 women with exertional angina, no LVH and flat ST slope. Kernel SHAP on the full model (train) ranks ca 0.149, sex:1 0.130, slope:2 0.121, cp:4 0.116, oldpeak 0.049, thal:7 0.046, chol 0.044 (mean |SHAP| on probability). Function preservation after the two input splits: max abs err 1.8e-15.
ann_31.proposed: Typical angina, non-anginal chest pain and atypical angina lower the predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms. More vessels coloured, a flat ST segment, more ST depression, a reversible thallium defect, higher cholesterol, older age and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy raise it; being a woman lowers it. The model ignores resting blood pressure.

ann_28.text: This part acts on 8 of 242 training patients (3%); nearly all of them are women and patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise.

For a typical patient it acts on, it raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 12% without this part to about 92% with it (on the training data only). The model has little data on this: only 8 training patients (patients the part acts on).
In the training data, 7 of these 8 patients had heart disease.

The model gives a clearly lower predicted risk of heart disease if the patient is a woman than if the patient is a man, and even more so if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy: for a typical patient, going from male to female moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 33% to about 1% if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy, and from about 23% to about 1% if resting ECG is something other than signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG.
